title: De compras
goal: Shop for clothes: name what you want, ask for a size and a price, and point things out.

lessons.title: Clothes
lessons.notes:
Clothes words are nouns like any other, so learn each with its article. To say what someone is wearing, use **llevar** (literally "to carry"): **Llevo una camiseta azul.** = I'm wearing a blue T-shirt.
Remember: colours come **after** the noun and agree with it: **una falda negra**, **unos zapatos negros**.
Some clothes are plural in Spanish, just as in English: **los pantalones** (trousers / pants), **los jeans**. In Spain jeans are **los vaqueros** and a jumper is **el jersey**.

items.note: Singular in Spanish: la ropa es nueva.

sentences.en: Today I'm wearing a white T-shirt.
accept_en: I'm wearing a white T-shirt today.
Today I wear a white T-shirt.

sentences.es: Ana lleva un vestido rojo muy bonito.
sentences.en: Ana is wearing a very pretty red dress.
accept_en: Ana is wearing a very nice red dress.
Ana wears a very pretty red dress.

sentences.en: I need some new shoes.
Where is my black jacket?

sentences.es: En el trabajo llevo camisa y pantalones.
sentences.en: At work I wear a shirt and trousers.
accept_en: At work I wear a shirt and pants.

sentences.en: My sister never wears a skirt.
In winter I wear a jumper.
accept_en: In winter I wear a sweater.
In the winter I wear a jumper.

sentences.es: Toda mi ropa está en la cama.
sentences.en: All my clothes are on the bed.

lessons.title: In the shop
lessons.notes:
**costar** (to cost) changes o -> ue, and you mostly need two forms:
**¿Cuánto cuesta?** (one thing) · **¿Cuánto cuestan?** (more than one)
**La talla** is the size of clothes; for shoes say **el número**: **¿Tiene el número 40?**
**probarse** (to try on) is reflexive and also o -> ue: **¿Puedo probarme la camisa?**
To pay: **pagar con tarjeta** (by card) or **en efectivo** (in cash). The shop assistant is **el dependiente / la dependienta**.

items.note: For clothes. For shoes: el número.

sentences.en: How much is the blue jacket?
accept_en: How much does the blue jacket cost?

sentences.en: How much are the black shoes?
accept_en: How much do the black shoes cost?

sentences.en: Do you have the shirt in a medium?
accept_en: Do you have the shirt in medium?
Do you have the shirt in a medium size?

sentences.en: Can I try on the green dress?
accept_en: May I try on the green dress?
Can I try the green dress on?

sentences.es: La falda es bonita, pero muy cara.
sentences.en: The skirt is pretty, but very expensive.
accept_en: The skirt is nice, but very expensive.

sentences.en: I want to buy some cheap trousers.
accept_en: I want to buy some cheap pants.
I want to buy cheap trousers.
I want to buy cheap pants.

sentences.en: Can I pay by card?
accept_en: Can I pay with a card?

sentences.en: No, in cash, please.
The T-shirt costs fifteen dollars.

lessons.title: This, that, that over there
lessons.notes:
Spanish points at things at three distances:
**este** (this - near me) · **ese** (that - near you) · **aquel** (that over there - far from both of us)
Each one agrees with the noun:
**este** suéter · **esta** falda · **estos** zapatos · **estas** camisas
**ese** vestido · **esa** chaqueta · **esos** pantalones · **esas** faldas
**aquel** carro · **aquella** tienda · **aquellos** zapatos · **aquellas** camisetas
Without a noun they mean "this one, that one": **Quiero este.** (Older books write éste with an accent; today it's optional and usually left off.)
Tip: in everyday talk **ese** often does the job of **aquel** too.

items.note: Careful: estás (you are) has an accent.

sentences.en: This jumper is very cheap.
How much is this skirt?
accept_en: How much does this skirt cost?

sentences.es: Estos zapatos son de mi hermano.
sentences.en: These shoes are my brother's.
accept_en: These shoes belong to my brother.

sentences.en: Do you like these shirts?
I like that dress.
That jacket is very expensive.
Can I try on those trousers?
accept_en: Can I try those trousers on?
Can I try on those pants?
May I try on those trousers?

sentences.es: Aquel carro rojo es de mi papá.
sentences.en: That red car over there is my dad's.
accept_en: That red car is my dad's.
That red car belongs to my dad.

sentences.en: Let's go to that shop over there.
accept_en: We're going to that shop over there.
Let's go to that store over there.

sentences.en: I don't want this one, I want that one.

lessons.title: Does it fit?
lessons.notes:
To say how clothes fit, Spanish uses **quedar** like **gustar**: the thing is the subject, the person is **me / te / le**.
**Me queda bien.** = It fits me well / It suits me.
**Te quedan grandes.** = They're too big for you (plural thing -> quedan).
**¿Cómo me queda?** = How does it look on me?
For shades, add **claro** (light) or **oscuro** (dark) after the colour, and these don't change: **una camisa azul claro**.
**le** works for él, ella and usted: **Le queda pequeño.** = It's too small for him / her / you.

items.note: Works like gustar: me queda, me quedan.

accept_en: they are too big for me

sentences.en: This shirt fits me well.
accept_en: This shirt looks good on me.

sentences.en: These shoes are too big for me.
accept_en: These shoes are big on me.

sentences.en: How does the coat look on me?
accept_en: How does the coat fit me?

sentences.es: Te queda muy bien ese color.
sentences.en: That colour really suits you.
accept_en: That colour looks very good on you.
That color suits you very well.

sentences.en: I want a dark blue jumper.
accept_en: I want a dark blue sweater.
I'd like a dark blue jumper.

sentences.es: Me gusta más la camisa verde claro.
sentences.en: I like the light green shirt better.
accept_en: I prefer the light green shirt.
I like the light green shirt more.

sentences.es: Al señor le queda pequeño el sombrero.
sentences.en: The hat is too small for the man.
accept_en: The hat is too small for the gentleman.
The hat is small on the man.

sentences.en: I need socks for the winter.

sentences.es: ¿De qué color es tu abrigo nuevo?
sentences.en: What colour is your new coat?
accept_en: What color is your new coat?
